title: Design and Construction of Artificial Extracellular Matrix (aECM) Proteins from Escherichia coli for Skin Tissue Engineering
protocol: Design the amino acid sequence of the functional domain including cell-binding and elastin-like repeats.
Select unique restriction sites flanking the ends of the functional domains.
Choose restriction sites present in the multiple cloning site (MCS) of the host vector for sub-cloning.
Reverse translate the amino acid sequence into the nucleotide sequence optimized for E. coli hosts.
Purchase gene of interest as single-stranded oligonucleotides if less than 100 base pairs.
Dissolve DNA oligonucleotides in a DNA oligomer buffer to a final concentration of 1 µg/µl.
Add 4 µl of each oligomer to 32 µl of DNA annealing buffer to create a total mixture of 40 µl.
Boil a beaker of water and immerse the 40 µl mixture for 5 min at 95 °C.
Remove the beaker from heat and cool the mixture gradually overnight in a Styrofoam box.
Add restriction enzymes, DNA, and buffer to digest annealed oligomers and pET22b(+) plasmid separately.
Incubate the digestion mixtures for 3-4 hours at 37 °C.
Add 6x loading dye to each digestion mixture.
Run the digestion mixtures on a 1.2% DNA agarose gel containing UV-fluorescent DNA stain for 1 hour at 100 V.
Visualize the 1.2% DNA agarose gel with a UV light illuminator.
Slice the gel to extract digested DNA products using commercial gel purification kits.
Elute the purified DNA using the minimum volume required to achieve a concentration of 50-100 ng/µl.
Ligate the digested DNA insert into the plasmid vector using T4 ligase according to the recipe provided.
Incubate the ligation mixture at room temperature for 2 hours.
Thaw E. coli DH5α chemically competent cells on ice.
Warm 2xYT agar plates containing ampicillin (25 µg/ml) to 37 °C.
Aliquot 50 μl of competent cells into clean, pre-chilled micro-centrifuge tubes.
Pipette 5 μl of the ligation mixture into the cells and mix gently up and down.
Leave the mixture on ice for 20 minutes.
Immerse the micro-centrifuge tube containing the cell mixture in a 42 °C water bath for 2 minutes.
Return the micro-centrifuge tube to ice for 2 minutes.
Add 500 μl of SOC media into the micro-centrifuge tube.
Incubate at 37 °C with shaking for 1 hour.
Spread 50 μl of the cell/ligation mixture onto a 2xYT agar plate containing ampicillin (25 µg/ml).
Incubate plates upside-down at 37 °C overnight (12-16 hr).
Pick DNA colonies from the agar plate using clean pipette tips.
Grow the colonies in 5 ml of 2YT media containing ampicillin (25 µg/ml) overnight at 37 °C with shaking (225 rpm).
Extract the DNA plasmids for each colony using a plasmid isolation kit according to manufacturer’s protocol.
Elute the DNA with 50 μl of water.
Mix 5 μl DNA, 0.2 µl of each restriction enzyme, and 1 µl 10x restriction enzyme buffer in a total volume of 10 μl for test digest.
Incubate the mixture at 37 °C for 2 hr.
Run the test digest on a 1.2% DNA agarose gel.
Send likely colonies for DNA sequencing using T7 promoter forward and reverse primers to commercial sequencers.
Thaw E. coli expression strain (BL21(DE3)pLysS) on ice.
Warm agar plates containing ampicillin and chloramphenicol to room temperature.
Wrap agar plates in Parafilm and store upside-down at 4°C for up to one month.
Pick a colony from the transformed agar plate with a pipette tip.
Inoculate into 10 ml of sterile Terrific Broth (TB) media containing ampicillin and chloramphenicol antibiotics.
Incubate starter culture at 37°C overnight with shaking at 225 rpm.
Transfer 10 ml of the starter culture into 1 L fresh and sterile TB media.
Supplement the TB media with antibiotics.
Incubate the culture at 37 °C with shaking at 225 rpm for 2-3 hr.
Pipette 1 ml of culture into an empty cuvette to measure optical density (OD600).
Prepare 1 vial of TB media in a cuvette as a blank measurement.
Transfer 1 ml of culture from the flask into a new empty cuvette.
Measure the optical density of the culture using a spectrophotometer at 600 nm against the blank control.
Save 1 ml of culture for subsequent SDS-PAGE analysis by transferring it to a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the sample at 12,000 x g for 2 min and decant supernatant.
Induce the culture with IPTG to achieve a final concentration of 1 mM.
Incubate the induced culture at 37 °C with shaking at 225 rpm for another 4 hr.
Save 1 ml of culture at the end of induction for SDS-PAGE analysis by transferring it to a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the sample at 12,000 x g for 2 min and decant supernatant.
Transfer the entire culture to 1 L centrifuge bottles.
Centrifuge the cultures at 12,000 x g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Weigh the cell pellets obtained from the centrifugation process.
Resuspend the cell pellets in TEN buffer (1 M Tris, 0.01 M EDTA, 0.1 M NaCl, pH = 8.0) at a concentration of 0.5 g/ml.
Freeze the re-suspended cell culture at -80 °C O/N.
Thaw the frozen cell culture in a water bath at RT or on ice to lyse the cells.
Add 10 μg/ml Deoxyribonuclease I (DNase I), 10 μg/ml Ribonuclease A (RNase I), and 50 μg/ml phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (PMSF) while thawing.
Homogenize the solution with slow stirring.
Adjust the solution to pH 9.0 to increase protein solubility in water.
Add 6 N NaOH drop wise with stirring on ice to achieve a homogenous consistency.
Lysate by ultrasonic disruption for 20 min on ice using a 2 mm diameter flat tip, 5 sec pulse.
Centrifuge the cell solution at 12,000 x g for 30 min at 4 °C.
Transfer the supernatant to a clean, empty bottle and store at 4 °C for purification later.
Resuspend the cell pellet again with TEN buffer and re-freeze at -80 °C.
Repeat freeze/thaw and sonication process up to three times.
Save 20 µl cell lysate for SDS-PAGE characterization.
Split the cell lysate into 50 ml centrifuge bottles.
Centrifuge the bottles at 40,000 x g for 2 hr at 4 °C.
Remove the supernatant by pipetting.
Add NaCl to a final concentration of 1 M (to a maximum of 3 M) and warm the solution to 37 °C for 2 hr with shaking at 225 rpm.
Centrifuge the supernatant from step 5.3 at 40,000 x g for 2 hr at 37 °C.
Decant the supernatant.
Crush the pellet using a metal spatula and resuspend in ice-cold autoclaved distilled water (50 mg/ml) with vigorous stirring O/N at 4 °C.
Repeat steps 5.2 to 5.4 for another three to five times to obtain higher purity of the protein.
Desalt the protein solution by dialyzing it against distilled water at 4 °C.
Dialyze protein solution against water for 2-3 days with changes in water every 4 hr or 8 hr for O/N.
Save 20 μl of the purified protein for SDS-PAGE.
Lyophilize the rest of the purified protein and store at -80 °C until further use.
Prepare a 12% SDS-PAGE gel.
Add 2x SDS loading buffer to each sample.
Heat samples for 10 min at 100 °C.
Run samples on the gel for 1 hr at 100 V or until the protein ladder reaches the middle of the gel.
Retrieve the gel from the SDS-PAGE setup.
Submerge the gel in Coomassie Brilliant Blue stain for 1 hr in a Petri dish.
Rinse the gel in a destaining solution for 5 min on a rocker.
Change the destaining solution and continue to destain until the background becomes clear.
Compare the position of the target protein against the protein ladder to determine its molecular weight.
Perform western blotting as described in step 7.
Cut nitrocellulose membrane to a size slightly larger than the SDS-PAGE gel.
Cut 4 pieces of filter paper to the same size.
Wet one piece of filter paper with Western Transfer Buffer (20% v/v methanol, 25 mM Tris, 190 mM Glycine, pH 8.3).
Place the SDS-PAGE gel on top of the wet filter paper.
Cover the SDS-PAGE gel with another piece of wet filter paper.
Position the nitrocellulose membrane over the gel and previous layer of filter paper.
Add a final two pieces of wet filter paper over the membrane setup.
Submerge the entire assembly with sufficient Western Transfer Buffer to ensure it is fully immersed.
Place two wet filter papers into a western semi-dry transfer unit.
Insert the nitrocellulose membrane onto the filter papers in the transfer unit.
Carefully place the SDS-PAGE gel within and on top of the membrane.
Add another two wet filter papers over the gel.
Run the western transfer at 45 mA for 30 minutes.
Monitor voltage; add buffer if it exceeds 30 V.
Retrieve the nitrocellulose membrane from the transfer unit.
Block the membrane with a blocking solution (5% non-fat milk in PBS pH 7.4, filtered) for 2 hours at room temperature.
Dispose of the blocking buffer and rinse the membrane with PBS.
Change gloves to avoid contaminating the membrane with unwanted proteins.
Incubate primary anti-His antibody with dilution in PBS at 1:1,000 at RT for 1 hr with rocking.
Prepare a mixture by adding 1 µl of antibody (stock concentration: 1 mg/ml) to 999 µl PBS for a total volume of 1 ml.
Rinse the membrane with 5 ml of PBST (PBS with 0.1% Tween20).
Incubate with secondary antibody conjugated to horse-radish peroxidase (HRP) with dilution in PBS at 1:5,000 at RT for 1 hr with rocking.
Prepare a mixture by adding 1 µl of antibody (stock concentration: 1 mg/ml) to 4,999 µl PBS for a total volume of 5 ml.
Wash the membrane with 5 ml of PBST and repeat twice.
Apply the chemiluminescent substrate to the membrane with a volume sufficient to cover the membrane.
Capture the chemiluminescent signals using a CCD camera based imager.
